change: Tightened height harmonization thresholds from 110%/88% to 105%/93%
lesson: Metric gaming: visual quality degraded despite score improvement. 'The' rendered as 'Tle'. Thresholds must not be tightened beyond 110%/88%.

change: Fold normalize/equalize/harmonize-height passes into one scale per word, one resample (same decisions, measured once on raw images)
expected: final ink heights within +/-1px for >= 90% of words; short all-body words keep dark ink; 'by' legible
lesson: Height prediction falsified: short words land 2-4px taller because int() truncation and ink-threshold erosion no longer shave pixels at each resample. Darkness was the wrong instrument (stroke-weight harmonization re-darkens everything); the damage was blur. Visual check: 'by' went from smudge to legible.

change: Remove 20%-from-median baseline clamp; word-aware detect_baseline (ink bottom for non-descender words, run-length body-below, relative walk-back)
expected: zero words more than 2px from their detected baseline after placement; 'they'd' right half on the body baseline

metrics_before.misdetected_baselines_seed42_137: by, they'd x2, it x2, for x2

lesson: The clamp compared row indices across canvases scaled by different factors. It raised exactly the words review 2026-04-19_215858 called superscript. Contact sheets with baselines drawn caught detector errors the density heuristics hid ('for' looked like a legitimate f-descender by numbers).

change: SIZING_POLICY zone (x-height matching via letter-class prior blended with measurement) vs total_height, generation held fixed from cache
expected: human prefers zone on >= 2 of 3 seeds in a blind pairwise A/B
lesson: Confirmed. The 2026-04-19 ruling that x-height is the wrong lever was confounded: both arms of that experiment carried the clamp bug. The human called this the first clear-cut choice in the review history; holding generation fixed and asking a pairwise question is what made it clear.

change: Re-run metric-human Spearman correlation at N=34 with held-out split at the 2026-04-10 selection date
expected: height_outlier_score keeps rho >= +0.2 on held-out reviews if it tracks preference
lesson: Failed replication. With ~16 metrics at p < 0.3, ~5 pass by chance. Gate replaced by x_height_consistency (human-validated by controlled A/B); require held-out replication before any correlation-selected metric gates.

change: detect_baseline: hybrid of density scan and body-band bottom for known descender words
expected: (recorded after the fact) band bottom fixes short descender words without moving long ones
lesson: Validate detectors on short words and several seeds, not just the demo text: round-1 contact sheets (demo text only) missed half the short-word failures. Scan fails low (in the descender), band fails high (thin round bottoms); the two failure directions make a cross-check work.

change: Local VLM judges (Qwen3.5-9B-AWQ, Qwen3-VL-8B-FP8) vs Claude subagent on 12 known-answer canaries + 3 human pairs
expected: (recorded after the fact) a 9B local VLM can stand in for the Claude judge on page A/B
lesson: Falsified. Local VLMs catch gross defects (blur, shouted words) but flip with A/B order on jitter and spacing: position bias, reasons parrot the rubric. Measure geometric defects deterministically (baseline_consistency, word_gap_ratio); keep the Claude judge for holistic calls; always judge both orders.

change: Word readers on 213 labeled crops: TrOCR-small, TrOCR-large, Qwen3.5-9B, Qwen3-VL-8B
expected: (recorded after the fact) a VLM reads short words better than TrOCR
lesson: VLM reader added as opt-in REFORGE_OCR_BACKEND=vlm. No reader detects misspelled renderings; legibility and letter fidelity are different instruments.

change: Best-of-N candidate selection and OCR retries scored by the local VLM reader instead of TrOCR-small (same seeds, identical first candidates)
expected: (recorded after the fact) the better reader selects better candidates

metrics_after.blind_claude_judge_prefers: trocr on 3/3 seeds (low, medium, low confidence)

lesson: Falsified. The VLM reads split, broken and overinked candidates as the intended word, so it stops filtering them; TrOCR's brittleness is a defect filter. Keep TrOCR for selection; the VLM backend is for legibility evaluation only.

change: Fresh-context Claude subagent as a spelling-defect rater on 213 word crops labeled with the intended spelling
expected: (recorded after the fact) Claude can replace by-eye spelling review
lesson: Claude on word sheets is a usable spelling-defect instrument between human sessions; no automated reader is.
